messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected for service=model-runner-prod across eu-west-1 and us-central-1. Trigger: error-rate > 5% for last 3m. Paging oncall.
maria: oncall here, grabbing it. pinging @ajay for runtime/serving help. :eyes:
ajay: ack. looking at traces and logs now. any customer-facing reports yet?
sam-cs: support queue shows ~8 customers reporting timeouts / 502s in last 10m. highest impact: customer=acme-inc, high-traffic route=/v1/generate. CS is notifying customers with a short message.
maria: good. to triage: can we confirm process-level crashes vs upstream gateway timeouts?
ajay: initial grep of model-runner logs shows repeated segfaults in model_runner process. snippets:
```
[2026-03-14T12:07:21Z] model_runner[pid=2345] ERROR: segfault at 0x7f8... in runtime::kv_cache::get
[2026-03-14T12:07:21Z] kernel: pid 2345 (model_runner), uid 1001: segfault at 7f8 ip 00007f8... sp 00007ff...
core dumped
```
ajay: also seeing OOM kills in some pods in us-central-1:
```
k8s evicted pod model-runner-5c7bb: eviction requested, memory pressure
```
maria: ok, sounds like memory pressure + occasional segfault. immediate mitigation options: 1) scale replicas out to drain burst, 2) temporarily disable large-batch path / reduce max_batch_size, 3) route traffic to fallback model variant (quantized) with lower mem footprint. thoughts?
leo: I'll take the scale path and handle k8s ops. @ajay can you prepare a safe config change to disable batching? if segfault is in batch path, that might stop crashes.
ajay: on it. creating a config patch to set `max_batch_size: 1` and `enable_batcher: false` for model-runner-prod. patch:
```
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/model-runner ENABLE_BATCHER=false MAX_BATCH_SIZE=1
```
ajay: also enabling `--no-prefetch-kv` on runtime to reduce memory usage.
eng-sre-bot: Action: scaling model-runner-prod from 6 -> 12 replicas in eu-west-1. Command: `kubectl -n prod scale deploy/model-runner --replicas=12` executed by leo at 12:09:40Z.
leo: scaled. pods coming up, but we have a backlog in the queue so some requests still failing until new pods are ready.
sophia: adding circuit-breaker rule at edge to fail fast for slow requests: set upstream timeout 10s and 429 on queue > 1000. Deploying via gateway now.
maria: thanks. ajay, any indicators whether segfault is deterministic for a particular model or request size?
ajay: reproducing locally with the same model and a prompt with long context (seq_len ~ 12k) leads to OOM in quantized attention kernel. Stacktrace points to cuda kernel launch failing then segfault. Sus suspect: kernel not handling large KV cache sizes properly.
```
(gdb) bt
#0  0x00007f8a... in runtime::attention::kv_update()
#1  0x00005555... in model::forward()
#2  0x00005555... in http_handler::handle_request()
```
maria: given that, routing traffic to the smaller-variant model is important. leo, can you add a routing rule to send requests > token_len 4096 to fallback-quantized? we should avoid sequence blowups.
leo: putting a canary policy in place: `route weight fallback-quantized=100` for the failing capacity zone (eu-west-1) until we confirm stability.
eng-sre-bot: Route update applied by leo at 12:15:02Z. New traffic split active.
sam-cs: CS update: we've notified impacted customers and posted status page note: "Investigating elevated errors for model inference in eu-west-1/us-central-1; mitigation in progress." Getting replies from Acme asking for ETA.
maria: ETA: immediate mitigations (scale + disable batching + route) should reduce errors within 5-10m. full fix will require runtime/kernel patch which may take days.
ajay: collecting core dumps from affected nodes and uploading to s3: `s3://redwood-incident-archives/1813001234/` — core files listed: core.model_runner.2345, core.model_runner.2890
ajay: quick workaround patch pushed to canary: fix bounds-check in kv_update to avoid out-of-range mem access; building a debug runtime rpm now. will roll to canary in ~30m after smoke tests.
leo: canary traffic to new runtime build? prefer to wait until we confirm no regressions. for now keeping fallback route and batcher disabled.
sophia: metric update: error-rate dropped from 8.7% -> 1.9% in eu-west-1 after routing and scaling. latencies increased slightly for some requests (p95 +80ms) but overall successful.
maria: good improvement. continuing monitoring. @sam-cs please post a short customer update saying we've mitigated most errors and are working on a permanent runtime patch.
sam-cs: posted. ticket numbers: INC-1813001234, CS-55432. customers notified.
eng-sre-bot: Reminder: on-call handoff in 40m. Maria, please update the incident channel with current state before handoff.
maria: noted. I'll prepare a handoff summary for next oncall.
ajay: logging next steps: 1) full root-cause analysis of kv cache growth w/ long context requests; 2) ship runtime patch with bounds check and safer allocation; 3) add stress tests for long context sequences; 4) revisit batching heuristics to prevent huge batch sizes combining long sequences.
leo: if we see reoccurrence after we re-enable batcher, we'll revert to routing fallback and roll back model-runner to known-good artifact.
maria: current status -> mitigation applied (scale, disable batcher, route fallback), error-rate reduced to ~1.5%, customer impact limited but visible for a subset. next updates in 20m or on new developments. handing to leo for next oncall coverage.
leo: taking over incident. I'll keep the channel updated. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident INC-1813001234 acknowledged by leo at 12:33:10Z. Priority: P1 -> P2 (mitigated). Logs and artifacts archived to s3.
